title: Inconsistent Naming of Identical Component Roles (Manager vs. Controller vs. Driver)
pattern: Using different role-suffix names (`Manager`, `Controller`, `Driver`, `Service`, `Executor`) interchangeably in the same codebase for components that share the same architectural and functional purpose.
why_bad: It violates uniform lexicon standards and breaks the principle of least surprise. Developers are forced to spend cognitive energy parsing whether a 'Manager' has structurally different behavior, lifecycles, or thread semantics compared to a 'Controller', when they are actually identical synonyms.
detection: Identify structs within the same package or layer that carry different role suffixes (e.g., matching both `*Manager` and `*Controller` in a struct-suffix scan) but have similar constructor signatures and lifetimes.
fix: Standardize on a single, well-defined suffix (e.g., renaming all components to `*Controller`) to maintain a single, cohesive design vocabulary.
source: *Clean Code* by Robert C. Martin (2008), p. 25, 292.
